title: English Adjective Errors Question Bank - Part 1
subject: English

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Anurag is eclipsed by his wife, (b) who is cleverer and (c) amusing than he is. (d) No error
options: Anurag is eclipsed by his wife,
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The adjective 'amusing' should be in the comparative degree 'more amusing' to maintain parallelism with 'cleverer'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The two first to arrive (b) were the lucky recipients (c) of a surprise gift. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'The two first' is incorrect word order. It should be 'The first two'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Of the billions of stars in the galaxy, (b) how much are (c) suitable for life? (d) No error
options: Of the billions of stars in the galaxy,
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Stars' is a countable noun, so 'how much' should be replaced with 'how many'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A few word of (b) gratitude are enough (c) to express your (d) feelings sincerely. (e) No error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'A few' is used with plural countable nouns. 'word' should be 'words'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He feels his troubles (b) as much or (c) even more than they. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The comparison is incomplete. It should be 'than they do' to properly compare the action of feeling troubles.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I like reading (b) more than (c) to play games. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Parallelism requires gerunds to be matched. 'to play' should be 'playing' to match 'reading'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There is not many traffic (b) along the street (c) where I live. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Traffic' is an uncountable noun, so 'many' should be replaced with 'much'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The police arrived and discovered (b) a large number of hoarded sugar (c) in his shop. (d) No error
options: a large number of hoarded sugar
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, so 'a large number of' should be 'a large amount of'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) As a dramatist (b) Shaw is superior than (c) any other twentieth century writer. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The adjective 'superior' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. It should be 'superior to'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Of the two great cities (b) the former is (c) biggest. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two items, the comparative degree 'bigger' must be used, not the superlative 'biggest'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A non banking financial company is a (b) financial institution similarly to a bank (c) but it cannot issue cheque books to customers. (d) No error
options: A non banking financial company is a
financial institution similarly to a bank
but it cannot issue cheque books to customers.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Similarly to' is incorrect here. The adjective 'similar' should be used: 'similar to a bank'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Everyone agrees that (b) the Ganga is the holiest (c) of all other rivers of India. (d) No error.
options: of all other rivers of India.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The Ganga is a river in India, so it cannot be the holiest of 'all other' rivers (which excludes it). It should be 'holiest of all rivers' or 'holier than all other rivers'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Krishna ran to the (b) nearing grocery store to (c) buy biscuits as his parents were expecting guests. (d) No error
options: buy biscuits as his parents were expecting guests.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Nearing' is a participle indicating motion towards. The correct adjective for location is 'nearby'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) While giving a loan (b) you must check (c) if the borrower has sufficiently collateral to repay it. (d) No error
options: if the borrower has sufficiently collateral to repay it.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Collateral' is a noun and requires an adjective modifier, not an adverb. 'Sufficiently' should be 'sufficient'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Although his speech (b) was not very clearly everyone understood (c) the underlying meaning. (d) No error
options: was not very clearly everyone understood
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After the linking verb 'was', an adjective is required, not an adverb. 'Clearly' should be 'clear'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He is the most (b) intelligent and also (c) the very talented student of the college. (d) No error
options: the very talented student of the college.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The phrasing is awkward and inconsistent. It should be 'the most talented' to parallel 'the most intelligent', or 'a very talented'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Having been found (b) guilty of the theft (c) Sunny was sentenced to five year's imprisonment. (d) No error
options: Sunny was sentenced to five year's imprisonment.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For a plural possessive, the apostrophe comes after the 's'. It should be 'five years' imprisonment'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The Railways have made (b) crossing the tracks (c) a punished offence. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: An offence that can be punished is a 'punishable' offence, not a 'punished' offence.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Alms (b) are given (c) to the poors. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When an adjective is used with 'the' to represent a class of people, it remains singular in form. 'Poors' should be 'poor'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Lasers are (b) indispensable tools (c) for the delicate eyes surgery. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a noun is used as an adjective (noun adjunct), it is typically singular. 'Eyes surgery' should be 'eye surgery'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The number of applications has risen (b) this year by (c) as many as 50%. (d) No error
options: The number of applications has risen
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: A percentage representing a singular amount or degree of increase takes 'much', not 'many'. It should be 'as much as 50%'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Two lakh of people (b) attended the meeting (c) held in parade ground. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a specific number precedes 'lakh', 'hundred', 'thousand', etc., 'of' is not used. It should be 'Two lakh people'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) These sort of men (b) attain success by hook or by crook (c) so they do not deserve any applause. (d) No error
options: attain success by hook or by crook
so they do not deserve any applause.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Sort' is singular, so it must be paired with the singular demonstrative 'This', not 'These'. It should be 'This sort of men'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Can you tell me how (b) many eggs and (c) milk he has brought (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Eggs' is countable (many), but 'milk' is uncountable and requires 'much'. The phrasing should be 'how many eggs and how much milk'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Whole the chapter (b) is full of printing errors which are the outcome (c) of the proof reader's carelessness. (d) No error
options: is full of printing errors which are the outcome
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct word order is 'The whole chapter', not 'Whole the chapter'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Her black long (b) hair adds (c) glamour to her looks. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In the order of adjectives, size/length comes before color. It should be 'long black hair'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I trembled when I saw (b) a sharp long knife (c) in his hand. (d) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Size/length ('long') should precede physical quality ('sharp'). It should be 'a long sharp knife'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) I saw (b) an anxious pale girl (c) who was fidgetting near the ICU (d) No error
options: who was fidgetting near the ICU
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Coordinate adjectives describing the same noun should be separated by a comma, or ordered strictly. 'Anxious, pale girl' is the correct punctuation and flow.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Mumbai is (b) further from (c) Delhi than (d) Patna. (e) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For physical, measurable distance, 'farther' is preferred over 'further' (which is for metaphorical or abstract degree).

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) This book is (b) undoubtedly preferable than (c) that and its printing (d) is also comparatively good. (e) No error
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The adjective 'preferable' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. It should be 'preferable to'.
